# Safe upstream synchronization and source-only Release mirror

AI-assisted downstream policy. Authorized scope: daily source synchronization and ordinary checks; mirror new formal upstream version tags, original release notes and source releases to this fork's GitHub Releases. **No compiled firmware is built or distributed by the scheduled release route.**

- `sync-upstream.yml` keeps the existing daily `43 4 * * *` schedule (04:43 UTC), non-destructive upstream merge and lightweight checks. The schedule runs inline policy tests; a GITHUB_TOKEN sync push does not trigger separate push workflows. Ordinary user push/PR pre-commit and policy checks remain enabled in YAML. Native validation workflows remain manually available; they are not publication assets.
- `source_mirror.py` only runs in `reliable-ly0411/ardupilot`, against `ArduPilot/ardupilot`. Drafts and prereleases are excluded. Existing Copter/Plane/Rover/Sub/Tracker family patterns (not AP_Periph), baseline `2026-10-20T13:55:00Z`, one release per run and maximum three automatic attempts remain unchanged. Historical releases are not backfilled.
- The operational ledger fixes upstream release ID, tag, peeled commit, publication date and notes digest. Retries reuse those values; changes fail closed. Explicit retry remains limited to an already failed/incomplete release.
- The downstream tag points at the **unchanged upstream commit**, not unreleased master or the downstream workflow patch. Same-name tags/releases are never overwritten. An identical existing release is accepted for recovery after a ledger-write interruption.
- GitHub's automatic source zip/tar archives provide the original source and licensing files. `COPYING.txt` must contain the upstream GPL notice. Submodule contents are not bundled by GitHub source archives: use a recursive clone for dependencies and their respective licenses. No binaries, test logs presented as binaries, signing keys or synthetic firmware assets are uploaded.
- Release notes reproduce the original upstream body beneath an explicit source-only notice, upstream URL, release ID, commit and date. They do not claim official downstream firmware, device validation or flight readiness.
- Original candidate validation/evidence tools are retained as manual-only legacy utilities. `promote-release.yml` remains blocked; it cannot publish old validation artifacts as firmware. The scheduled source route does not call it or `release-build.yml`.
- No websites, package registries, R2 writes/deletes, issue/PR closure, comments, labels or new credentials are used. Existing credential/security restrictions and fork side-effect guards remain in place.

Validation: `python3 -m unittest discover -s .github/release_policy -p 'test_*.py' -v` and `python3 -m py_compile .github/release_policy/*.py`. Tests mock publication APIs; they do not create public releases. The manual `sync` action can validate live synchronization without invoking source publication.

## All upstream branches and tags

The daily job synchronizes every advertised upstream branch and tag, not only `master`. Its manual `sync` action does the same synchronization without inspecting or publishing source Releases. The existing `check-releases` action and scheduled source-only Release policy above remain unchanged.

- The job runs only for this fork and `refs/heads/master`, using its existing short-lived repository `GITHUB_TOKEN` with `contents: write`. It does not need a personal token or any new secret. The shared `release-policy-master` concurrency group prevents overlapping synchronization and release-policy runs.
- GitHub can reject a ref update that introduces workflow-file content outside this token's permissions. `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot receive the separate `workflows` permission through workflow YAML. Such a rejection stops the atomic transaction and needs operator review; this implementation does not replace the token, add credentials or change protection rules. Using a different credential would also need a separate review of push-triggered workflows on copied upstream branches.
- Lightweight tests run before any write. The existing master merge is prepared locally while preserving downstream workflow and release-policy files; conflicts outside those paths require manual resolution. The master update is not pushed separately.
- New upstream branches are copied exactly. Other shared branches only fast-forward; downstream commits already ahead of upstream are preserved. A diverged branch stops synchronization for review. Fork-only branches, including the release ledger, are not deleted or reset.
- New tags retain the exact upstream Git object, including annotated or nested tag metadata and signatures. Existing fixed version tags are never overwritten, even when both objects resolve to the same commit.
- Only the established `beta` and `stable` aliases for APMrover2, AP_Periph, AntennaTracker, ArduCopter (including heli), ArduPlane and ArduSub may move. Each old direct object is retained under a fresh `sync-backup/rolling/<tag>/<old-object-id>-<transaction-id>` ref before and with the update. Every move requires a newly created backup in the same atomic transaction, rather than relying on a no-op update to an existing backup. A backup name or namespace collision stops the job. All earlier recovery tags, including `sync-backup/2026-11-08/`, are retained.
- The prepared master, branch updates, tags and new backups are sent in one atomic push, each with an explicit expected old object or an expectation that the ref is absent. Changed snapshots, tag conflicts, stale leases, protection rules or missing atomic-push support stop the operation without a destructive fallback. There is no mirror, prune or delete operation.
- Ref snapshots and direct object IDs are verified after the push. A failure or uncertain result needs inspection before any retry. The Actions log reports synchronization results and preserved downstream branches; actual scheduled execution must be checked in the Actions run history.

`sync_refs.py --expected-master <pre-merge-master-sha>` produces a read-only plan by default; `--apply` performs the guarded transaction. Its tests use isolated local bare repositories and exercise object fidelity, branch/tag conflicts, recovery refs and concurrent updates without contacting GitHub or creating Releases. No upstream build scripts or firmware builds run as part of synchronization.
